timed_text.text: Day 27.
One question to carry for the rest of your career.
What's next?
Not what did I achieve?
What's next?
Here's why this matters.
One of the biggest performance killers in sport: complacency after success.
You make the team, hit a personal best — and your standards quietly drop.
Because part of your brain thinks the job is done.
The, what's next habit prevents that.
Continuous growth — setting new limits the moment you reach the old ones.
Sustaining elite performance: never satisfied with what you built.
They used each achievement as a launching pad for the next standard.
Three days from completing this. Here's the most important thing:
Finishing is not the goal, the next chapter it is.
On your screen you're going to answer the prompted question.

cards.prompt: What have you built over the last 27 days that you didn't have when you started?
What is the next standard you're committing to? Not a wish — a specific, behavioral commitment that starts the day after this program ends.
What's next? Write it as a declaration. 'After this program, I commit to...'

timed_text.text: What's next?
Keep asking that question.
Every achievement, every season, every milestone.
The answer to that question is where the growth lives.
Now that you're finished, day 27 is complete.
